title: Review: Cell theory, microscopes and magnification; Cell specialisation, tissues, organs; Dissection and tissue studies; Membrane structure (fluid mosaic)
specRef: CC2(c), CC2-SP1, CC2-SP2, C2.4-SP3 and others; CC2(d); CC2-SP2, C2.2-SP1, C2.2-SP2; ...

Terms and clues: PR05a#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE01a#t3 term and clue written for the game; MB01a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE01a#N.12, CE07a#N.11, MB01a#N.7, PR05b#N.11, CE01a#N.9, CE07a#N.3a, MB01a#N.3a, CE01a#N.6, CE07a#N.10b, MB01a#N.10a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Annotation
items.clue: A label plus a short note on what a structure does or a feature you can see.

items.label: Phospholipid
items.clue: Molecule with a charged, water-loving head and two non-polar fatty acid tails.

items.label: Eyepiece graticule
items.clue: Scale seen down the microscope whose divisions have no fixed size until calibrated

items.label: Hydrophobic
items.clue: Describes non-polar parts, such as fatty acid tails, that are kept away from water.

questions.stem: A micrograph shows a pollen grain 60 mm across. A scale bar on the micrograph is 20 mm long and is labelled 10 µm. What is the actual diameter of the pollen grain?

options.text: 3 µm
30 µm
60 µm
120 µm

questions.explanation: Magnification = 20 000 µm ÷ 10 µm = ×2000. Actual size = 60 000 µm ÷ 2000 = 30 µm.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of plant, leaf cells make large amounts of a protein that binds chlorophyll, but the root cells of the same plant make none of it. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: In root cells, the base sequence of the gene has been changed, and the gene no longer codes for the protein.
Both cell types carry the gene for the protein, but it is expressed in leaf cells and not in root cells.
Root cells have lost the gene for the protein from their DNA because they did not use it.
Root cells do not need the protein, so they choose not to make it, unlike the cells of leaves.

questions.stem: Which statement about glycoproteins in the plasma membrane is correct?

options.text: Their carbohydrate is on the extracellular side and is used in cell recognition and adhesion.
Their carbohydrate is on the cytoplasmic side and is respired when the cell lacks glucose.
Their carbohydrate projects from both faces of the membrane so that either face can be recognised.
They are transport proteins whose carbohydrate forms the channel through which sugars enter the cell.

questions.explanation: Glycoproteins are proteins with a carbohydrate chain attached. The carbohydrate faces outwards, where it works in cell recognition and cell adhesion.

questions.stem: A student dissects a set of sheep's lungs. Near the lungs she finds two tubes side by side. Tube P has C-shaped rings of cartilage in its wall and stays open when empty. Tube Q has a thin, soft wall with no cartilage and collapses flat. Which identification do these observations best support?

options.text: P is an artery: it has the thicker wall and stays open, as arteries do.
P is a bronchus, held open by its cartilage; Q is a blood vessel.
Q is an artery: blood at high pressure needs a wide, soft-walled vessel.
Q is a vein, because it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.explanation: Structure identifies it: C-shaped cartilage keeps airways open. A thin wall that collapses fits a vein, such as a pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: With the ×40 objective lens in place, 40 divisions of an eyepiece graticule line up exactly with 100 µm on a stage micrometer. Using the same objective, a cell spans 44 graticule divisions. What is the actual length of the cell in millimetres?

options.text: 1.1 mm

questions.explanation: 100 µm ÷ 40 = 2.5 µm per division with this objective. 44 × 2.5 µm = 110 µm = 0.11 mm.

questions.stem: In a human, a neuron and a liver cell are both descended by mitosis from the same zygote. What is the difference between them once they have differentiated?

options.text: They express different subsets of the same complete set of genes.
They have kept different sets of genes and discarded the rest.
They were set on different paths inside from fertilisation.
They differ only until the body needs to swap them over.

questions.explanation: All cells produced by mitosis from the zygote inherit the full genome. The neuron switches on the genes for its proteins and the liver cell a different set, while both keep every gene.

questions.stem: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer when they are mixed with water?

options.text: Enzymes in the cell join the phospholipids together into a sheet, using energy released from ATP.
The whole molecule repels water, so the phospholipids gather away from it as a droplet of oil.
Covalent bonds form between neighbouring phospholipids, linking them into one rigid sheet of molecules.
Hydrophilic heads face the water and hydrophobic tails are shielded from it, so the sheet forms spontaneously.

questions.explanation: In water the most stable arrangement is a continuous sheet two molecules thick, heads towards the water on both sides and tails in the middle. It forms with no energy input.

questions.stem: In a photomicrograph taken at a magnification of ×2000, a red blood cell measures 15 mm across. What is the actual width of the cell?

options.text: 7.5 µm

questions.explanation: Actual size = 15 mm ÷ 2000 = 0.0075 mm, which is 7.5 µm (1 mm = 1000 µm): the typical diameter of a red blood cell.

questions.stem: The wall of the stomach contains epithelium, smooth muscle and connective tissue. Together they digest and churn food. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue are each organs, as each has a function.
The stomach is an organ system, as it contains several different tissues.
The stomach is an organ: several tissues working together for an overall function.
Epithelium is not a tissue if it contains goblet cells as well as other cells.

questions.explanation: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue each do one job; together they perform digestion, the stomach's overall function.

questions.stem: A student draws a two-dimensional representation of the fluid mosaic model. Which feature of the drawing is correct?

options.text: The tails of the inner layer point into the cytoplasm, as the cytoplasm is the inside of the cell.
The proteins are drawn at regular, equal spacings, like tiles set in a fixed pattern across the sheet.
Glycoproteins are drawn with their carbohydrate chains on the cytoplasmic side of the membrane.
Cholesterol is drawn among the phospholipids within the bilayer, not on its surface.

questions.explanation: Cholesterol sits within the bilayer among the phospholipids. The hydrophilic heads form both surfaces and the hydrophobic tails form the core.
